title: Finite-Tor domains for closed coefficient change
statement: For the same finite coefficient datum, closed immersion and finite-Tor input, scalar extension and both closed exceptional outputs satisfy the three finite-Tor constructibility conclusions appearing in finiteCoefficientClosedShriek.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–3; strict subclaim extracted for stage-3 decomposition

proof.text: Extract an ordered Tor interval [a,b] from the intrinsic finite-Tor input. Conjugate the given lifted coefficient homomorphism by ULift.ringEquiv to obtain a homomorphism of the original coefficient rings; its lift equals the original map by extensionality. Apply closedScalarDomains_scalar and take its finite-Tor membership component to obtain the scalar-extended input.

For either coefficient stage, use intrinsic_bc_realization_iff and intrinsic_hasProEtaleTorAmplitude_iff_torAmplitudeIn to express the input as a fixed-module bounded constructible finite-Tor object. The coefficient prime is invertible in D.k: recover characteristic p from the finite-field cardinality and use l distinct from p. The finite coefficient quotient therefore has invertible exponent. Apply the existing upstream ProEtale.constructibleFiniteTor_rightDerivedUpperShriek to the proper closed immersion. Its functor is definitionally sfFiniteExceptionalFixed for the chosen proper compactification. Transport constructibility and Tor amplitude back to the intrinsic predicate. Widen any output interval [c,d] to [min c d,d] before using the ordered intrinsic interval comparison.

Apply the exceptional preservation argument to M over E. Extract its Tor interval and apply closedScalarDomains_scalar on Z to obtain scalar extension of the E-exceptional output. Apply exceptional preservation independently over L to the already scalar-extended input. Assemble the three membership proofs by conjunction introduction.

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraphs 1–3; use existing scalar-domain and upstream exceptional-preservation theorems, with intrinsic predicate transport.

lean.statement: theorem finiteClosedShriek_domainPart (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : l ≠ D.p) (E L : Type u) [Field E] [Field L] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] [Algebra (Padic l) L] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) L] (m n : ℕ) (φ : ULift.{u + 1, u} (splitCoefficientDomain l E m) →+* ULift.{u + 1, u} (splitCoefficientDomain l L n)) (X Z : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))) [IsSeparated X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] [IsSeparated Z.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Z.hom] [QuasiCompact Z.hom] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i.left] (M : splitDerivedDomain X.left (splitCoefficientDomain l E m)) (_hM : finiteTorConstructibleProEtaleModule l E (m + 1) (Nat.succ_pos m) X.left M) : finiteTorConstructibleProEtaleModule l L (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) X.left ((splitScalarDomain φ X.left).obj M) ∧ finiteTorConstructibleProEtaleModule l L (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) Z.left ((splitScalarDomain φ Z.left).obj ((splitExceptionalDomain (splitCoefficientDomain l E m) i.left).obj M)) ∧ finiteTorConstructibleProEtaleModule l L (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) Z.left ((splitExceptionalDomain (splitCoefficientDomain l L n) i.left).obj ((splitScalarDomain φ X.left).obj M))
